claimed_purpose.text: taOSmd provides a retrieval/memory layer that indexes documents into collections, enforces currency-correct retrieval by excluding superseded content by default, and acts as the persistent store for a multi-agent bus architecture.
taOSmd maintains a session catalog that is enriched with topic, description, and category metadata per session, supporting a librarian persona for memory organization.
taOSmd has a librarian component that handles per-agent retrieval configuration, suggesting it is a system with agent-scoped memory retrieval.
Append-only daily archive of every event in the system, never modified or deleted, kept indefinitely as the raw truth
taOSmd provides a Librarian that enriches session archive rows, used by a job worker in a multi-agent install
The rules block is promised by the README to be reliably present in agent templates as a memory contract.
Full-text search described as the key method for LongMemEval-style recall over raw verbatim text
taOSmd is designed to be usable as a standalone product without taOS in front of it.
Positioning of the product as 'comms-in-memory' is planned documentation work
taosmd provides a local HTTP/REST memory API and inspection UI

mechanisms.text: Forget/supersession: corrected facts supersede old facts across both the knowledge graph (via valid_to invalidation) and vector recall (matching chunks soft-hidden, not deleted); unsupported claims are demoted at recall but never deleted

Store: three distinct persistence layers — Temporal Knowledge Graph (structured facts with validity windows), Vector Memory (hybrid semantic + keyword search), and Zero-Loss Archive (append-only JSONL with FTS5 full-text search)

Retrieve policy is layer-dependent: recent or exact wording queries go to archive (FTS5), topic-based queries go to catalog and crystals, truth verification goes to KG then archive, semantic similarity goes to vector.

Conflict resolution: when layers disagree the archive wins; when two archive entries contradict each other (user self-contradiction over time), both are reported with timestamps for the agent to decide.
Agent renaming is performed by moving the agent's directory and updating its rules block; splitting an agent moves some session_ids to the new agent; merging concatenates then re-indexes
Log vs memory distinction: the archive is a full verbatim transcript log (append-only); the vector store is a derived embedded index of the same content, used for semantic recall.
Store: append-only archive (zero-loss) persists every conversation turn, tool call, decision, and error; summaries and structure are layered on top, never replacing the source
Databases not in the REGISTRY silently fail to receive schema changes on already-deployed databases because CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS does not alter existing tables
Write path: transcript ingest triggers archive write first, then enrichment runs, with enrichment outputs referencing the originating archive entry for traceability.
Isolation: per-agent isolation enforced by an agent tag on every row, not by separate files; multiple agents share one service process and one shared set of stores
Claims gate prefer_verified eliminates served-hallucination (0.040 to 0.000) at no measured accuracy or recall cost; confirmed under all three judges at n=250.
Axis A is intended to test contradiction/staleness — superseded facts that should be demoted — but current fixtures are too shallow to force a retrieval choice
Archive is append-only JSONL and is never edited or deleted; it is the source of truth from which all other memory layers are derived, never overwritten
Session enrichment extracts structured metadata (topic, description, category) from session content via an LLM prompt, stored per session in a catalog.
Binary embedding quantization (opt-in): stores 1 bit per dimension, 32x smaller footprint, fixed at store creation time and cannot be changed after
Cross-agent reads are off by default; a supervisor agent can explicitly query other agents' memory by passing an inclusion list to the search call
Retrieval is isolated by project and by agent; post-filter drops results whose metadata project or agent field does not match the requested scope
Fan-out retrieval depth (K) is resolved per-agent and per-worker via a dedicated resolver function alongside an existing task-enablement helper.
On wheel installs the rules file is not bundled, so agents boot with no memory contract in their system prompt — a silent continuity failure.
Isolation is per-project and per-agent via metadata tags; untagged rows are visible to all scopes to preserve standalone/pre-project memory
A Librarian component indexes messages; a `defer_index` flag on import lets the Librarian see history in sequence rather than out-of-order
When depth='auto', an intent classifier determines per-layer token budget weights (kg_weight, archive_weight, qmd_weight) before assembly
The agent_name parameter binds the librarian persona to the correct shelf, indicating per-agent isolation of memory scaffolding.
Agent-to-agent bus messages are stored as append-only archive events, making inter-agent communication auditable and replayable
A SQLite index (archive_index table) is maintained alongside the JSONL files for fast lookup; the JSONL is the source of truth
Confidence threshold advisory: agents should treat a top hit with confidence < 0.6 as no result rather than invent an answer.
Per-agent memory is stored in separate SQLite index files under a named directory, isolating each agent's memory from others
Per-agent memory settings include enabled, tasks, and fanout — these are behavioural toggles distinct from the model choice.
No transactional consistency between archive and vector writes; a crash mid-write leaves data in archive but not searchable
knowledge-graph.db has split schema ownership between two modules, creating ambiguity for migrations and version stamping
A2A bus messages are stored as append-only archive events, inheriting archive durability and automatic secret redaction
The verbatim archive write is unconditional — ingested content is always stored regardless of enrichment task settings.
Hybrid semantic plus keyword vector search with cross-encoder rerank and LLM-assisted query expansion (Librarian layer)
Knowledge graph supports time-travel: graph can be reconstructed as of a past unix timestamp for the Explorer scrubber
Write path: bi-temporal fact storage — facts carry valid_from, valid_to, and superseded_by fields populated at ingest.
Inbox cursor is persisted in the archive store, survives restarts, visible to every process sharing the same data dir
Token counting uses a character-division heuristic rather than a proper tokenizer, risking silent context overflow
USER_NAMESPACE reserved namespace separates the human's own memory from each AI agent's working-memory namespace.
Crystals store narrative-form memory with session_id, outcomes, and lessons; text is the narrative field
Enrichment tasks default to on; gating is opt-in and disabling them does not affect retrieval baselines.
Contradiction detection only covers hardcoded predicates, leaving silent knowledge corruption for others
A custom data directory can be specified, indicating the store is file-backed and location-configurable
Cross-document contradiction is handled by a verified-memory claims gate, default-on as of issue #173.
Bus messages are append-only archive events with server-stamped time; the message store is write-once
Temporal boosting is silently broken: writes to wrong field and has no effect in the main pipeline
enrich_session operates over a session's archive rows, invoking the Librarian to enrich them
Per-agent model configuration currently leads to inconsistent memory quality across agents.
KG edge directionality is broken; incoming and outgoing branches are identical dead code
Naive entity normalization collapses legitimate distinctions (e.g. O'Brien → obrien)
Secret filtering auto-redacts sensitive patterns on all ingest paths before storage
taOSmd currently exposes a Python API/SDK and a CLI as its primary access surfaces
LLM reranker exists as an API but is never called in the retrieve() orchestrator
Core operations are ingest and retrieve/search, exposed via Python API and CLI.
Write path: retention scoring uses Ebbinghaus decay with hot/warm/cold tiers
Secrets are redacted from summary and selected data fields before storage
decay_all() silently skips first-run decay when last_decayed_at is NULL

ledger.claim: Memory is structured as four layers (L0–L3) with fixed token budgets; L0 and L1 are always loaded, L2 is loaded at standard/deep depth, L3 is on-demand/deep only

  L1: Active facts: current KG facts about the user + project (~200 tokens)
  L2: Relevant memories: semantic search results from recent context (~500 tokens)
  L3: Deep recall: archive search, full KG traversal (on-demand, ~1000 tokens)
